title: Kung Pao Chicken & Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Kung Pao Chicken & Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Braised chicken thighs in a tangy soy-vinegar kung pao sauce with peanuts and scallions over rice
subtitle: Braised chicken thighs in a tangy soy-vinegar kung pao sauce with peanuts and scallions over rice
description: Chicken thigh chunks braise directly in a tangy soy-vinegar-chili kung pao sauce with garlic and ginger until tender and glossy, served over rice with roasted peanuts and scallions scattered on fresh at the table for crunch.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse and cook jasmine rice per package directions; fluff and hold covered while the braise comes together.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add chicken chunks and brown 5–6 minutes until golden outside—it will finish cooking in the braise.

steps.title: Bloom chilies and aromatics
steps.instruction: Push chicken to one side, add remaining oil, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns; stir 30 seconds until fragrant and the oil turns red. Add garlic and ginger, stir 20 seconds more.

steps.title: Braise in the sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch, and broth; pour over the chicken. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 12–15 minutes until chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened and turned glossy.

steps.title: Finish with peanuts and scallions
steps.instruction: Off heat, stir in peanuts and scallions right before serving so they stay crunchy, not soft. Serve over rice.

proTips: The dried chilies are for aroma, not necessarily for eating—warn the crew not to bite into them whole.
Cashews work as a substitute if peanuts aren't on hand.
This braises hands-off—no need to watch it every second the way a wok stir-fry demands.
tonightSpread: Quick cucumber salad with rice vinegar.
leftovers: Reheats beautifully on the stove or microwave—braised thighs don't turn rubbery the way stir-fried breast can.
Chop into fried rice with leftover jasmine rice.
whyCrewsLikeIt: All the sweet-tangy-savory kung pao flavor the crew already loves, minus the flash-wok timing pressure—this one simmers, holds, and reheats like a real braise. Peanuts added fresh at the end keep the crunch nobody expects from a healthy dinner.
mealPrepNotes: This braises hands-off once it's going—stir occasionally but there's no wok-timing pressure. Add peanuts only at serving so they stay crunchy. Station: Brown the chicken first for flavor, then let the sauce actually simmer—this is a braise, not a flash stir-fry. Station: Add peanuts and scallions fresh at serving, not during cooking, so they don't go soft sitting in the sauce. Station: If a call interrupts mid-simmer, cover and hold on low—kung pao only gets better with extra time.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos. Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon.
